records.text: White has a new passed pawn. That means no enemy pawn stands ahead on its file or the neighboring files; pieces may still stop it.
Black has a new passed pawn. That means no enemy pawn stands ahead on its file or the neighboring files; pieces may still stop it.
The better move would have created a passed pawn for White. No enemy pawn would stand ahead on its own or neighboring files.
The better move would have created a passed pawn for Black. No enemy pawn would stand ahead on its own or neighboring files.
White's pawn is isolated now: no friendly pawns occupy the adjacent files. Any support it has must come from pieces.
Black's pawn is isolated now: no friendly pawns occupy the adjacent files. Any support it has must come from pieces.
With the better move, White would have an isolated pawn. Piece support could still exist, despite the lack of neighboring friendly pawns.
With the better move, Black would have an isolated pawn. Piece support could still exist, despite the lack of neighboring friendly pawns.
White now has doubled pawns, sharing a file. Their arrangement matters, but it doesn't by itself make the position bad.
Black now has doubled pawns, sharing a file. Their arrangement matters, but it doesn't by itself make the position bad.
The stronger alternative would leave White with doubled pawns. Those pawns would share a file; the rest of the position still matters.
The stronger alternative would leave Black with doubled pawns. Those pawns would share a file; the rest of the position still matters.
White's rook has an open file now, with no pawns of either color on it. Pieces can still limit the rook's movement.
Black's rook has an open file now, with no pawns of either color on it. Pieces can still limit the rook's movement.
The better move would give White's rook an open file. That describes the absence of pawns, not the absence of every obstacle.
The better move would give Black's rook an open file. That describes the absence of pawns, not the absence of every obstacle.
White's rook now has a semi-open file. Its own pawns are absent from that file, while enemy pawns remain.
Black's rook now has a semi-open file. Its own pawns are absent from that file, while enemy pawns remain.
The better alternative would give White's rook a semi-open file. Friendly pawns would be absent from it, but enemy pawns would remain.
The better alternative would give Black's rook a semi-open file. Friendly pawns would be absent from it, but enemy pawns would remain.
White's knight was undefended before the move. It now has a defender; that is a change in support, not a guarantee of safety.
Black's knight was undefended before the move. It now has a defender; that is a change in support, not a guarantee of safety.
Notice the support for White's bishop. It had no defender before, and this move gives it one.
Notice the support for Black's bishop. It had no defender before, and this move gives it one.
White's rook has gained a defender after having none. Keep that new connection in mind when examining captures.
Black's rook has gained a defender after having none. Keep that new connection in mind when examining captures.
The queen's support has changed: White's queen was undefended and now has a defender.
The queen's support has changed: Black's queen was undefended and now has a defender.
The better move would give White's knight a defender where it had none. A defender is support, not a guarantee of safety.
The better move would give Black's knight a defender where it had none. A defender is support, not a guarantee of safety.
White's bishop would gain a defender with the alternative move. It was undefended before that proposed move.
Black's bishop would gain a defender with the alternative move. It was undefended before that proposed move.
The stronger alternative would add support to White's undefended rook. The resulting position would include a defender for it.
The stronger alternative would add support to Black's undefended rook. The resulting position would include a defender for it.
Another move would give White's queen a defender. It lacked that support before the move.
Another move would give Black's queen a defender. It lacked that support before the move.
White's knight has lost its last defender. Being undefended does not establish that a capture is available.
Black's knight has lost its last defender. Being undefended does not establish that a capture is available.
This move leaves White's bishop without the support it had. No defender remains, though that doesn't prove the bishop is lost.
This move leaves Black's bishop without the support it had. No defender remains, though that doesn't prove the bishop is lost.
White's rook is now undefended, having lost its last defender. Check the possible replies before judging the consequence.
Black's rook is now undefended, having lost its last defender. Check the possible replies before judging the consequence.
White's queen no longer has a defender. That describes its support; an actual capture needs its own examination.
Black's queen no longer has a defender. That describes its support; an actual capture needs its own examination.
The better move would leave White's knight undefended. Losing its last defender would not automatically mean losing the knight.
The better move would leave Black's knight undefended. Losing its last defender would not automatically mean losing the knight.
White's bishop would lose its remaining support in the alternative. It would have no defender after that move.
Black's bishop would lose its remaining support in the alternative. It would have no defender after that move.
With the stronger alternative, White's rook would lose its last defender. That fact alone wouldn't prove a material loss.
With the stronger alternative, Black's rook would lose its last defender. That fact alone wouldn't prove a material loss.
Another move would leave White's queen without any defender. The absence of support and a winning capture are different claims.
Another move would leave Black's queen without any defender. The absence of support and a winning capture are different claims.
The knight had not left its original square before. This first move out is what development means here.
The knight develops here by leaving its starting square for the first time. Now examine what it can do from the new square.
Until this move, the knight had stayed where it began. Its first departure is a step in development.
The knight develops by leaving its starting square for the first time. Begin by examining the squares it can reach from here.
The bishop begins its development with this first move from home. Follow its diagonals from the new square.
A bishop has developed here. It has left its starting square for the first time, so examine its new placement.
Before this move, the bishop hadn't left home. Its first move away from the starting square begins its development.
The bishop's first departure from its original square is the development detail here. The next question is how it fits the position.
The stronger alternative would develop a knight by moving it off its original square for the first time.
The knight hadn't yet left its starting square. With the better move, it would have made that first departure.
Developing a knight was available in the alternative: its first move from the square where it began the game.
With another move, a knight would have begun its development. It would leave its original square for the first time.
A bishop would have developed with the stronger choice, moving off its original square for the first time.
The better move would have been the bishop's first departure from its starting square. Compare that placement with the game.
The alternative included developing a bishop. It would have left the square where it began the game for the first time.
The bishop had not yet moved from its original square. The stronger alternative would have changed that.
Compare the position after this move with the position after the stronger choice. This one is worse for the side that moved.
The cost belongs to the choice between these moves. The stronger alternative would have left a better position.
This choice falls short of the best move. Put that move on the board, then compare the replies available to each.
A move can give something up in the evaluation without losing a piece. Here, the played move is worse than the stronger alternative.
The opponent has a capture available immediately. A legal capture and a profitable capture are different things, so examine the result.
After this move, the other side can capture at once. That is a concrete reply to include in the analysis.
No preparation is needed for the other side's capture. It is already available on the next move.
The next reply can be a capture. Follow what happens after it before deciding whether it wins anything.
You made use of the opponent's previous error. The important connection is between that mistake and your response.
Their last move offered an opportunity, and you acted on it. That's successful punishment of the error.
Your reply turns the opponent's mistake to use. Notice how the opportunity and the response fit together.
The better alternative would leave a stronger position than the move played.
There was a stronger choice available; compare its result with this position.
Another move would have done better, which gives a useful basis for comparison.
The pawn was already passed before this move. It has now advanced closer to promotion, though it may still be stopped.
This is an advance of an existing passed pawn. It is nearer the promotion rank now; the possible defenses still need checking.
The strongest reply puts the king in check. Any response has to deal with that check.
Check is the best answer to this move. Examine the legal ways to meet it before considering another plan.
You played the intended move for this lesson. Keep that step in mind as the lesson continues.
Correct for this lesson. That's the move being taught at this point.
That matches the lesson's intended choice. Nicely followed.
You found the correct move. The puzzle continues, so give the next position the same attention.
This part of the solution is correct. There are more moves to find before the puzzle is complete.
Good, that move is right for the puzzle. Continue with the next position.
Your move matches the opening you're practicing. That's the recall being checked here.
Correct for your chosen repertoire. You recalled the move in the study line.
That is the move your opening material gives for this position. Nicely remembered.
Best. This is the strongest choice here; understanding it is useful even without an error to correct.
This move earns Best. Take time to understand it, just as with a move that needs correcting.
Good. The move is sound, while a stronger choice was available. Both facts matter.
This is a sound move, graded Good. Studying the best alternative can still add to the understanding of it.
